entries.name: Temporal Residual
entries.mixing: Original backbone plus a cross-token residual
entries.composition: Each attention or FFN sublayer can read and write one carried residual stream.
entries.state: One fixed-width carried vector in addition to the base model’s cache and recurrent states.
entries.summary: Adds a second residual stream that survives from one token to the next. The retrofit starts as the original model and learns how strongly each sublayer should read or write the carried state.
entries.novelty: Unlike Recycler or temporal middle-layer recurrence, feedback is not injected into the original residual alone. Unlike Latent Lattice, a shared carry passes through the network rather than maintaining independent per-layer time states.
entries.evidence: Adds 2,752 parameters to Qwen3.5-4B-Base. After 5B adaptation tokens, AIME 2024/2025 improve by 7/13 points over the same-data baseline; the math advantage persists at matched compute.
entries.limits: One base model; the broader suite’s advantage does not survive compute matching. Parallel training approximates the sequential carry, and lower training-mode loss did not reliably predict decoding accuracy.

diagram.caption: Sublayers read and write the carry before it moves to the next token.

entries.name: LimeTree
entries.mixing: Tree message passing with multiscale memory
entries.composition: Gated bottom-up aggregation, skip paths over tree levels, and top-down refinement.
entries.state: A multiscale memory bank; linear memory in sequence length, not fixed-size recurrent state.
entries.summary: Organizes the token sequence as trees and exchanges learned messages across their levels to build language context.
entries.novelty: Rather than choose a sparse mask over token-to-token attention, it makes multiscale tree nodes and learned message passing the main substrate for representing history.
entries.evidence: The author reports WikiText-103 perplexity of 19 and full recall on the synthetic KV probe at 16,384 positions after training at 512.
entries.limits: Training explicitly includes synthetic retrieval exercises. Context extrapolation on that probe does not establish equal recall on natural long documents; the two corpora use different configurations.

diagram.caption: Leaves are aggregated upward; coarse summaries also refine lower nodes.

entries.name: Access-First Global Workspace
entries.composition: Four specialist modules with four internal rounds per generated token.
entries.state: Private states plus one shared packet per round; these states reset per generated token.
entries.summary: Specialist modules exchange information through a single learned broadcast, then use it to query their own private memories.
entries.novelty: The workspace is the only inter-module route, and the decoder cannot read it directly. That lets interventions distinguish a receiver’s own computation from simply relaying an answer.
entries.evidence: A workspace-message swap made models emit the answer predicted by recombination in about 97% of the tested synthetic cases.
entries.limits: A small, purpose-built diagnostic with assigned module roles; it is not a pretrained general-purpose language model.

diagram.caption: One shared packet redirects what each recipient retrieves.

entries.name: Clover / BD-GDN
entries.mixing: Gated DeltaNet state + local bidirectional softmax
entries.composition: 30 block-diffusion GDN mixers and 10 full-attention layers; sparse FFNs.
entries.state: Fixed-size recurrent history in GDN layers; full-attention layers still retain KV.
entries.summary: A query-specific recurrent prefix read competes with noisy in-block tokens in a shared softmax. Only committed tokens update the recurrent state.
entries.novelty: Changes the Qwen3.6 causal mixer itself: recurrent writes to the clean prefix are separated from bidirectional, jointly normalized reads during denoising.
entries.evidence: The authors report 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 680 tokens/s on one GB300 for an internal replay workload.
entries.limits: No matched ablation isolates the mixer from training and decoding changes. Replay speed is system-level throughput and does not measure task success.

diagram.caption: The prefix state is held fixed while the active block is denoised.

entries.name: Latent Lattice
entries.mixing: Backbone mixer conditioned by recurrent companion states
entries.composition: Vertical residual through depth; separate horizontal recurrence at each participating layer.
entries.state: Fixed-width state per participating layer in addition to the backbone’s original memory.
entries.summary: Gives layers their own latent state across tokens. The state steers queries, cache writes, MLPs, and the readout instead of replacing the sequence mixer.
entries.novelty: A GDN or Mamba state is the mixer’s memory. Here, the carry sits beside the mixer and shapes how that mixer and the rest of the layer compute.
entries.evidence: At about 406M parameters and 20B training tokens, the authors report FineWeb-Edu perplexity of 14.40 versus 15.41 for a matched Transformer.
entries.limits: Sub-billion language models and 2K training context. Optional nonlinear top-to-bottom refinement costs extra sweeps; the simpler version keeps the parallel scan.

diagram.caption: Each participating layer reuses its own state at the next token.

entries.name: Concertina
entries.mixing: Causal attention with token-conditioned step corrections
entries.composition: Groups of adjacent teacher layers become repeated shared blocks with gated low-rank deltas.
entries.state: Retains teacher-depth attention computation and KV cache; saves parameter storage.
entries.summary: Folds nearby layers of a pretrained model into repeated blocks, preserving layer-specific behavior with low-rank corrections.
entries.novelty: Relative to static depth-wise adaptation in the Relaxed Recursive Transformer, each token can blend corrections derived from the original adjacent layers.
entries.evidence: The authors report 84% mean recovery relative to Qwen3-4B on eight benchmarks after 22B distillation tokens.
entries.limits: Tested only in the Qwen3 family; folding does not shrink effective depth or the KV cache, and serving latency was not measured.

diagram.caption: Each pass uses the same base weights with token-routed corrections.

entries.name: NCP / ArchPreview
entries.composition: Token encoder, product quantizer, concept predictor and token decoder with residual routing.
entries.state: One concept per four tokens in the preview; the token stream is retained.
entries.summary: Learns and predicts a discrete vocabulary of multi-token concepts. Predicted concepts feed back into token generation.
entries.novelty: Unlike a larger subword vocabulary or a standalone text compressor, the concept alphabet is learned from hidden states and receives its own next-concept target.
entries.evidence: The preview trained on 5.73T tokens and reports +2.45 points on its downstream average over OLMo-3-7B.
entries.limits: The headline comparison is against a smaller model; simultaneous parameter and compute controls are shorter experiments. The preview uses fixed concept length.

diagram.caption: A dedicated module predicts the next concept before it guides token generation.

entries.name: LoGo
entries.composition: Sliding-window attention for every query, with selected queries allowed to read the full prefix.
entries.state: Dense KV cache remains; sparsity targets attention computation.
entries.summary: Learns which tokens need full-context attention and uses the cheaper sliding window for the rest.
entries.novelty: Where static hybrids allocate global attention by layer or head, LoGo allocates it by query token without approximating full attention for the selected queries.
entries.evidence: At 1.5B, the 128K checkpoint reports 65.4 average RULER versus 58.5 for the best static comparator.
entries.limits: No reduction in dense KV storage. Wall-clock gains are sensitive to kernel quality and the proportion of queries routed globally.

diagram.caption: The routing decision controls which queries are granted full-context reads.

entries.name: BitNet b1.58
entries.composition: Transformer decoder with BitLinear projections trained for ternary arithmetic.
entries.state: Ternary weight storage does not eliminate the attention KV cache.
entries.summary: Trains the model natively around projection weights in {−1, 0, +1}.
entries.novelty: Native ternary training changes the arithmetic the model learns to use; it is not an after-the-fact conversion of a dense checkpoint.
entries.evidence: The follow-up 2B4T report releases a 2B checkpoint trained on 4T tokens and provides matched-size evaluations and specialized inference implementations.
entries.limits: Not all tensors are ternary. Deployment advantages depend on kernels and hardware; they cannot be inferred from the weight alphabet alone.

diagram.caption: Training incorporates ternary projections rather than quantizing a finished model.

entries.name: RWKV-7 Goose
entries.composition: Recurrent time mixing followed by channel mixing.
entries.state: Matrix state per head; no growing token-level KV cache in recurrent inference.
entries.summary: Updates a running matrix memory with input-dependent dynamics rather than revisiting a stored sequence of keys and values.
entries.novelty: Extends the earlier RWKV recurrence from simple retention toward a more expressive delta-style state transition with in-context memory control.
entries.evidence: The paper evaluates a 2.9B model on multilingual and English benchmarks and reports strong results for that scale.
entries.limits: Constant-size state is not perfect recall. Benchmark comparisons do not match all data and training budgets.

diagram.caption: The memory matrix is updated instead of appending a token to a cache.

entries.name: LLaDA
entries.context: Generation uses a chosen response length
entries.composition: A Transformer predicts masked positions across a response canvas over multiple rounds.
entries.state: The partly denoised sequence is revisited across passes; no standard append-only AR cache.
entries.summary: Starts from masked output positions and fills them by repeated denoising rather than committing to a left-to-right generation order.
entries.novelty: Masked diffusion predates LLaDA; this is a from-scratch 8B-scale demonstration of that alternative factorization as a general-purpose LM.
entries.evidence: The authors compare the 8B model against self-trained autoregressive baselines over language, code and math tasks.
entries.limits: Parallel predictions do not guarantee lower end-to-end latency; repeated full-sequence work and length choices matter.

diagram.caption: Several output positions can be predicted across each denoising round.

entries.name: Huginn / Recurrent Depth
entries.context: Token sequence retained across depth loops
entries.mixing: Attention inside a shared recurrent core
entries.composition: Prelude, repeated middle block, and coda.
entries.state: Latent representations update across depth; attention still needs token-level memory.
entries.summary: Applies a weight-shared block multiple times to token representations so inference can spend more compute without emitting more reasoning tokens.
entries.novelty: It makes recurrent depth a language-model test-time compute knob at multi-billion scale, building on earlier Universal Transformer-style weight sharing.
entries.evidence: The paper reports improvements with additional latent iterations on selected math and reasoning evaluations.
entries.limits: More iterations still cost compute; gains vary by task and are not guaranteed at arbitrary loop counts.

diagram.caption: Depth iterations refine hidden state before the next token is sampled.

entries.name: Byte Latent Transformer
entries.mixing: Local byte operations + patch-level global attention
entries.composition: Local byte encoder, global patch Transformer, and local byte decoder.
entries.state: Global attention operates on patches, so its history grows with patch count rather than byte count.
entries.summary: Groups raw bytes into variable-length patches and runs most compute over those patches rather than a fixed subword vocabulary.
entries.novelty: Compared with fixed-size byte grouping, an entropy-based boundary rule spends more global compute where the bytes are harder to predict.
entries.evidence: The paper reports scaling runs up to 8B parameters and compares quality and compute with tokenized baselines.
entries.limits: Patch rate depends on the text, and the entropy model plus local encode/decode add work. Compression is not a fixed ratio.

diagram.caption: The expensive global model runs over the irregular patch sequence.

entries.name: Test-Time Training Layers
entries.mixing: Fast weights updated by a self-supervised loss
entries.composition: A linear model or small MLP serves as the trainable hidden state inside the sequence mixer.
entries.state: Sequence-specific, mutable fast weights; separate from the slow model parameters.
entries.summary: Makes the recurrent state a small model, updated as that model learns to reconstruct views of the input.
entries.novelty: Compared with conventional fixed-form recurrent updates, the write is a learning step on an internal objective, allowing the hidden state to encode a learned function.
entries.evidence: The paper compares TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP language models with Transformers and Mamba up to 1.3B parameters.
entries.limits: The inner gradient work adds implementation costs; larger fast-weight models were bottlenecked by memory I/O.

diagram.caption: The inner learning step changes the memory used by later positions.

entries.name: Mamba
entries.composition: Selective state-space mixer with local convolution and gating in repeated blocks.
entries.state: Fixed-size SSM and convolution state; no growing attention KV cache.
entries.summary: Selectively writes, retains and reads information from an SSM state using parameters derived from the current input.
entries.novelty: Unlike earlier time-invariant SSMs, token-dependent transitions let the mixer choose what to remember. A hardware-aware scan recovers parallel training.
entries.evidence: The original report evaluates language models up to 3B parameters as well as audio and genomics sequence models.
entries.limits: Linear sequence cost does not establish exact retrieval or universal superiority over softmax attention.

diagram.caption: Current input controls the state transition and what the layer reads out.
